measurement: evidentia-measure-book, BSB source with no Strong tag of its own, --without-source-strong --learn-from KJV (Mark adds --learn-from-strong-numbers), final tier = global review + syntax-gated target gloss, at essenthos-core wt/goldscore
note: Word and link ids are this database load's and do not survive a reload; reference, position and surface are the stable key. Nothing here is applied to the corpus or to the answer key: every published EVIDENTIA figure is still scored against the rows as loaded.

dataset: Berean Standard Bible translation tables, bereanbible.com, public domain
errors.why: BSB 'lifted the ark high above the earth': 'high' is the only rendering of וַתָּרָם 'and it rose', which the Berean table leaves unlinked while putting 'high above' on מֵעַל. מֵעַל means 'from upon', not 'high'; the chunk joins a word from one Hebrew clause to the preposition of another.

dataset: Berean Standard Bible translation tables, bereanbible.com, public domain
errors.why: 'so that we may not perish' = וְלֹא נֹאבֵד. The Berean table links 'so that' to וְ+לֹא and 'we may not perish' to נֹאבֵד alone, so the negative is stated as the rendering of 'so that'. No reading makes לֹא 'so that'; 'not' -> לֹא is right.

dataset: Clear Bible Alignments, BiblioNexus, github.com/Clear-Bible/Alignments, CC BY 4.0
errors.why: Not the annotators. The stored Clear Bible row says 'a baptism' -> μετανοίας, and every link after 'appeared' in Mark 1:4 is one Greek word late ('preaching' -> βάπτισμα, 'repentance' -> εἰς). Clear Bible's own record aligns the BSB words to BGNT 9 κηρύσσων and 10 βάπτισμα; BGNT reads καὶ κηρύσσων where Nestle 1904 has no καί, and the corpus joins BGNT words to Nestle 1904 by position.

dataset: Clear Bible Alignments, BiblioNexus, github.com/Clear-Bible/Alignments, CC BY 4.0
